name: Fibre-optic connector
summary: A demountable joint between optical fibres, drawn as a connector on a fibre link with an optical path mark.
description: The fibre-optic connector shows a point where two fibres are joined by a demountable connector, such as at a patch panel or on a relay communications port. Protection signalling and process bus networks use many of them, and each one adds insertion loss to the link budget.

The symbol does not state the connector type, polish or whether it is single mode or multimode. Mismatched connectors or polish types cause high loss or reflections. Fusion splices are a different item and should not be drawn as connectors, since they cannot be disconnected.
readingNotes: Count connectors on the link for the loss budget.
Check connector type against the device port.
drawingChecklist: Record connector positions in the fibre schedule.
distinction: A fibre-optic connector is demountable; a fusion splice is a permanent joint.
